tasks.title: Standardize unified auth API surface (types, methods, errors)
tasks.description: Define provider-agnostic API: auth.api.getSession, authClient.signUp/email/signIn/magicLink/signOut/getSession, organization.acceptInvitation; unify User/Session/AuthError shapes; unify { data, error } results with stable error codes.

subtasks.title: Define common User and Session interfaces
subtasks.description: Create standardized interfaces for User and Session objects that will work across all auth providers. Ensure these interfaces contain all necessary fields while abstracting provider-specific details.
subtasks.details: Define TypeScript interfaces for User (id, email, name, etc.) and Session (user, token, expiresAt, etc.) that can be implemented by both Better-Auth and Supabase. Consider existing usage patterns in the application to ensure backward compatibility. Include proper JSDoc comments for all interface properties.

subtasks.title: Define AuthError types and error code system
subtasks.description: Create a unified error handling system with consistent error codes that work across providers. Define the AuthError class structure and standardize error codes for common auth failures.
subtasks.details: Design an AuthError class with properties for code, message, and optional cause. Create an enum of stable error codes (e.g., INVALID_CREDENTIALS, EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED, SESSION_EXPIRED) that will remain consistent regardless of the underlying provider. Map provider-specific errors to these standardized codes. Document each error code with expected scenarios and recommended user-facing messages.

subtasks.title: Standardize auth API method signatures
subtasks.description: Define consistent method signatures for all auth operations including signUp, signIn, signOut, getSession, and organization-related methods that will work across providers.
subtasks.details: Create TypeScript interface definitions for all auth methods: auth.api.getSession, authClient.signUp, authClient.signInWithEmail, authClient.signInWithMagicLink, authClient.signOut, authClient.getSession, organization.acceptInvitation, etc. Ensure parameters and return types are consistent and use the User/Session interfaces and error handling patterns defined earlier. Document each method with JSDoc comments including parameters, return values, and possible errors.

subtasks.title: Implement unified result pattern with { data, error }
subtasks.description: Create a standardized result envelope pattern that returns { data, error } for all auth operations, ensuring consistent error handling across the application.
subtasks.details: Define a generic AuthResult<T> type that follows the { data?: T, error?: AuthError } pattern. Update all API method signatures to return this type. Create utility functions for creating success and error results. Ensure the pattern handles null/undefined cases properly and provides type safety. Document best practices for consuming these results in application code.

subtasks.title: Document the unified auth API contract
subtasks.description: Create comprehensive documentation for the standardized auth API including interfaces, methods, error codes, and usage examples to serve as the contract for implementations.
subtasks.details: Produce detailed documentation covering: 1) All User/Session interface properties, 2) Complete list of error codes with explanations, 3) Method signatures with parameters and return types, 4) Usage examples for common flows (signup, login, etc.), 5) Guidelines for error handling, and 6) Migration notes for updating existing code. Include diagrams showing the relationship between components and the authentication flow.

subtasks.description: Implement Hono middleware that supports both cookie-based and bearer token authentication for Supabase

subtasks.title: Implement Supabase-specific cookie management
subtasks.description: Create utilities for handling Supabase authentication cookies across different environments
subtasks.details:
Develop cookie management utilities specific to Supabase that handle setting, retrieving, and clearing authentication cookies. Implement proper security measures for cookies including appropriate flags (HttpOnly, SameSite, Secure). Ensure consistent cookie behavior across SSR, client-side, and middleware contexts.
<info added on 2025-09-26T07:19:06.593Z>
Supabase cookie management should be centralized in middleware and SSR server client implementations using only the cookies.getAll and cookies.setAll methods provided by @supabase/ssr. No custom cookie utilities need to be developed as Supabase's built-in cookie management functions are sufficient for handling authentication cookies with proper security measures. This approach ensures consistent cookie behavior across SSR, client-side, and middleware contexts while adhering to Supabase's recommended implementation patterns.
</info added on 2025-09-26T07:19:06.593Z>

tasks.title: RLS policies and indexes verification for app tables
tasks.description: Ensure RLS policies are defined per operation with auth.uid() and necessary indexes exist. Use declarative schema and rules.

subtasks.title: Audit existing tables for RLS policies
subtasks.description: Review all application tables to verify they have appropriate Row Level Security policies that use auth.uid() for user-specific access control.
subtasks.details: Create a comprehensive list of all tables in the database schema. For each table, document existing RLS policies, noting whether they properly use auth.uid() for authentication. Flag any tables missing RLS policies or using incorrect authentication methods. Pay special attention to tables with sensitive data.

subtasks.title: Implement missing or correct existing RLS policies
subtasks.description: Create or modify RLS policies to ensure each operation type (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) has separate policies using auth.uid() for proper authorization.
subtasks.details: Based on the audit results, write declarative schema definitions for missing RLS policies. Ensure each operation type has its own policy rather than using ALL. Follow the pattern: CREATE POLICY "policy_name" ON table_name FOR operation TO authenticated USING (auth.uid() = user_id). Document any special cases where different policy logic is required.

subtasks.title: Add necessary indexes to support RLS queries
subtasks.description: Identify and create indexes on columns referenced in RLS policies to ensure efficient query performance when policies are applied.
subtasks.details: Review all RLS policies to identify columns used in policy conditions (especially foreign keys and user_id columns). Create appropriate indexes on these columns if they don't already exist. Test query performance with EXPLAIN ANALYZE before and after index creation to verify improvements. Document all indexes in the schema definition files.
